function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

### How Turbonomics Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability | Goal | What Turbonomics Provides | Why It Matters for Unilever | |------|---------------------------|-----------------------------| | **Unified Visibility Across All Clouds** | • A single pane of glass that aggregates metrics from GCP, AWS, Azure, on‑prem, and edge environments.
• Real‑time dashboards that surface performance, cost, and capacity across all workloads. | Unilever can see the health of its global supply‑chain, marketing, and retail analytics workloads without switching between vendor consoles. | | **AI‑Driven Decision Making** | • Machine‑learning models that predict resource utilization, cost spikes, and potential bottlenecks.
• Automated “what‑if” simulations to evaluate the impact of scaling or re‑allocating resources. | Enables proactive optimization—Unilever can avoid over‑provisioning expensive compute for seasonal demand spikes or under‑provisioning during product launches. | | **Cost Optimization & Budget Control** | • Continuous cost monitoring with alerts when spend deviates from budget.
• Recommendations for rightsizing, spot/low‑priority instance usage, and reserved‑instance purchases. | Helps Unilever keep cloud spend in line with corporate sustainability targets while ensuring performance for critical business processes. | | **Policy‑Based Governance** | • Declarative policies that enforce compliance, security, and cost limits across all clouds.
• Automated remediation (e.g., shutting down idle VMs). | Simplifies governance across multiple teams and regions, reducing manual effort and risk of non‑compliance. | | **Self‑Healing & Auto‑Scaling** | • AI‑driven auto‑scaling that reacts to real‑time workload changes.
• Self‑healing actions that restart or migrate workloads if performance degrades. | Keeps Unilever’s e‑commerce, analytics, and IoT platforms highly available during peak traffic periods. | | **Integration with Existing Tooling** | • APIs and connectors for Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD pipelines, and monitoring tools like Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog. | Allows Unilever to embed Turbonomics insights into existing DevOps workflows without reinventing the wheel. | #### Practical Use Cases for Unilever 1. **Seasonal Demand Forecasting** * Turbonomics predicts CPU/memory needs for the holiday season and automatically scales up the relevant microservices across AWS and Azure. 2. **Sustainability Reporting** * AI models identify low‑utilization resources and recommend shutting them down, helping Unilever meet carbon‑footprint reduction goals. 3. **Multi‑Region Retail Analytics** * Unified dashboards show latency and throughput for analytics workloads running in GCP, AWS, and Azure, enabling quick root‑cause analysis when a region lags. --- ### Difference Between Turbonomics and Native Cloud Provider Tools | Feature | Turbonomics | GCP Native Tools (e.g., Cloud Monitoring, Cost Management) | AWS Native Tools (e.g., CloudWatch, Cost Explorer) | Azure Native Tools (e.g., Monitor, Advisor) | |---------|-------------|----------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------| | **Scope** | Cross‑cloud (multi‑cloud + on‑prem) | Single‑cloud | Single‑cloud | Single‑cloud | | **Unified Dashboard** | One UI for all clouds | Separate consoles per provider | Separate consoles per provider | Separate consoles per provider | | **AI/ML Capabilities** | Predictive analytics, automated recommendations, self‑healing | Limited predictive features; mostly rule‑based alerts | Limited predictive features; mostly rule‑based alerts | Limited predictive features; mostly rule‑based alerts | | **Cost Optimization** | Continuous, automated rightsizing, spot‑instance recommendations, policy enforcement | Manual cost analysis, budgeting, some automated recommendations | Manual cost analysis, budgeting, some automated recommendations | Manual cost analysis, budgeting, some automated recommendations | | **Policy Enforcement** | Declarative policies that span clouds, automated remediation | Policies limited to each provider’s ecosystem | Policies limited to each provider’s ecosystem | Policies limited to each provider’s ecosystem | | **Automation & Orchestration** | API‑first, integrates with Terraform, Kubernetes, CI/CD | Limited automation; mostly manual or provider‑specific scripts | Limited automation; mostly manual or provider‑specific scripts | Limited automation; mostly manual or provider‑specific scripts | | **Self‑Healing** | AI‑driven auto‑scaling and remediation across clouds | Rule‑based auto‑scaling within a provider | Rule‑based auto‑scaling within a provider | Rule‑based auto‑scaling within a provider | | **Vendor Lock‑In** | Vendor‑agnostic | Vendor‑specific | Vendor‑specific | Vendor‑specific | #### Bottom Line - **Turbonomics** gives Unilever a *single, AI‑powered view* that cuts through the complexity of managing workloads across GCP, AWS, Azure, and on‑prem environments. - Native tools are powerful but *provider‑centric*;
